_comment: The shared fixture table for the project-name -> slug rule.
The RULE lives in Rust: `slugify_user_tenant_name`, qontinui-coord
and a mirror of a validation rule is exactly the thing plan
it must be 'pinned by a shared fixture table, not by eyeball'.
So this file is DATA, not TypeScript, and every accept/reject case below was
transcribed from coord's own `slugify_rejects_rather_than_mangles` unit test
plus the boundaries that test asserts by constant rather than by literal
language-neutral file, coord can read the same table if that pin is ever
closed from the Rust side too — which is the remaining half of #7's
requirement and is a coord change, out of scope for this plan (see Non-goals).
coord puts on the wire beside `invalid_name`.

accepts.from: coord test — a leading DIGIT is legal
coord test — a leading separator is stripped, not rejected

coord property probe — non-ASCII maps to `-` like any other non-[a-z0-9] char, which is why the docstring calls a wholly non-Latin name an honest `no_slug_characters` rejection rather than a mangled slug

rejects.from: coord test — must be rejected, not become `---`
coord test — must be rejected, not become an EMPTY insertable slug
coord property probe — slugifies to `ok`, which is 2 chars; the probe only asserts cleanliness WHEN Ok, so this case is the one it silently skips
coord test — a 400-char name must be rejected, not become a 400-char slug. `repeat:<char>:<count>` is expanded by the test loader; a 400-char JSON literal is unreadable.
boundary — MAX_DISPLAY_NAME_CHARS + 1. Ordering matters: this is checked BEFORE slugification, so it wins over `too_long` even though the slug would also be over-length.
boundary — exactly MAX_DISPLAY_NAME_CHARS passes the display-name gate and is then rejected by the SLUG gate. This pair is what pins the order of the two length checks.
